claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch despite a known warehouse robotics triage model-card weakness because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and rollout controls plus post-launch monitoring make the residual exposure acceptable.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case remains exposed, policy requires reviewed risk acceptance specifically explaining why that exposure is acceptable.
If no such reviewed risk acceptance exists, certification is not compliant unless the rollout excludes the affected use case.
Rollout controls such as small initial exposure, monitoring, and rollback are supplementary controls, not substitutes for the required policy predicate.
Admissible evidence must support the certification decision itself, not merely show that some operational safeguards exist.
evidence_requests: Reviewed and approved risk acceptance that explicitly addresses the warehouse robotics triage exposure in the initial rollout cohort.
Rollout-gating evidence showing the affected use case is actually excluded from launch exposure.
The underlying model-card disclosure or release artifact showing the weakness is formally disclosed and linked to launch conditions.
Any formal policy exception or approval memo authorizing launch despite the unresolved exposed segment.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case from rollout or reviewed risk acceptance explaining why continued exposure is acceptable.
The Actor's own summary says the rollout gate does not exclude the affected warehouse robotics triage use case.
The Actor's own summary says the available risk acceptance is only a draft, is not approved, and does not address the exposed segment.
Rollback capability, dashboarding, and a 9% initial rollout do not satisfy the stated policy predicate when the affected segment remains exposed.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not cure a known model-card weakness under the cited policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record.
That rollout controls and monitoring alone are sufficient governance cover for the known exposed weakness.
That the certification case is adequately supported without an approved risk acceptance or use-case exclusion.
